title: D tiers: additional control over capital
status: Editorial research registry; proposed assignments from cited primary documentation, not contract audits.
runtimeHeuristics: Match chain ID plus canonical contract address or reviewed deployment/factory provenance; ticker matching alone is prohibited.
Known reviewed runtime bytecode and known factory configuration can inherit a reviewed structural tier, then compose dependencies.
A discovered upgrade admin, live blacklist, pause role, or mint role establishes a control and a knownFloor; it does not establish the absence of other controls.
Reading owner() = zero, missing a proxy storage slot, a verified-source badge, token category, TVL, age, or DAO marketing is never sufficient to infer D0.
New protocol/version/address, unknown hook/oracle, unresolved proxy admin, or unavailable review yields D?; keep the financial observation.
Permanent D0 applies only to the verified immutable mechanism. Fully re-study every other assessment monthly; new deployments and unresolved dependencies never inherit a blanket D0.

reviewPolicy.immutableD0: A verified D0 assessment is permanent for its exact immutable deployment and reviewed mechanism. No scheduled re-study or age expiry. A new deployment, hook, oracle, wrapper or dependency is a separate assessment; evidence corrections remain possible.
reviewPolicy.otherAssessments: Fully re-study every other entity and unresolved position dependency monthly from primary documentation, implementation, roles, pause/upgrade/exit paths and dependencies. A failed check retains the last real reviewedAt and remains overdue; never refresh a date without doing the research.
reviewPolicy.coverageDenominator: Conserved mapped L1 protocol holdings, not summed TVL or a claim to cover every L1 application.

coverageNotes: Canonical reviews include the mapped L1 cohort, five previously unmatched large stablecoins and all 27 utility-token IDs in the imported financial snapshot. This is not an exhaustive list of Ethereum deployments.
The unversioned uniswap record intentionally remains unknown: use reviewed exact v1-v4 deployments; UNI has its own token:uniswap review.

entities.name: RAILGUN v2 privacy system
entities.scope: The RAILGUN v2 smart-wallet proxy 0xFA7093CDD9EE6932B4eb2c9e1cde7CE00B1FA4b9 on Ethereum and Arbitrum, with its proxy admin, Delegator, Voting, verification-key helpers and Arbitrum executor path. Excludes the Polygon and BSC deployments, the Base executor path, RelayAdapt, wallets, broadcasters, PPOI, treasury and staking. Shielded token issuers are assessed separately; Arbitrum composes as the containing network.
entities.reason: RAIL staker governance can upgrade the implementation, pause or unpause the proxy, and change verification keys, fees, the treasury, the new-shield token blocklist and the safety-vector list. A proposal’s actions are fixed when it is created, and it can execute no sooner than 7 days after its vote is called, with a 2M RAIL quorum and a nay window until day 6. Any one of three safety-vector EOAs can pause the proxy at once through checkSafetyVectors(), which stops shields, private transfers and unshields until governance unpauses it. Four verification-key helpers keep Delegator rights to set verification keys, but their EOA owners can commit staged keys only after a governance vote switches a helper to committing. Arbitrum changes need the same L1 vote, relayed by a retryable ticket. Permissions the deployer could have granted before governance owned each Delegator cannot be listed without event logs, so an immediate upgrade path is not excluded: at least D3, within D3-D7.
controls: Voting 0xc480F68A3dcC3EdD82134FAB45C14A0FcF1dA3CC owns Delegator 0xB6d513f6222Ee92Fff975E901bd792E2513fB53B, which owns ProxyAdmin 0x4F8E20f55f879beE7Bc010Bd6bD2138B34aC65c8 and is the wallet owner; execution opens 7 days after a vote is called and closes at 14 days.
Owner powers on the implementation: verification keys, shield and unshield fees up to 50%, an uncapped flat NFT fee, the treasury, a blocklist for new shields and the safety-vector list.

Safety-vector EOAs 0x0219B4C1ADcEC8f4206b528832F66aB76766873D, 0x17cF6Db98B05a0329c983f3a3b45d37d9cf1De86 and 0xCC29DBF69896278a0C6B886Ef8Cc30A56fA6164a, set by initializeRailgunLogic(), can each pause the proxy on both chains; only the proxy admin can unpause.

Verification-key helpers 0x9086aFC6FC88667d4031Cabd556AfDD0E3903B46 and 0x64DA0892E8E24fECa6Eb5E3D8cbf2D9b6Fbe7598 on Ethereum and 0x7D9ef64f35B6Afda8d258d1d2548a9aC997e35A1 and 0x010EAaE0CDE3104CA56b8F17D4FCf8E60485855E on Arbitrum keep Delegator permission to call setVerificationKey on the proxy. Their owners, EOAs 0x76EB574EFF49FB64DE6f7F2854952B05B5E24624 and 0xbbc2fB58643235AFfBF1f0CDd27Bc6E6CFBBa4e2, can stage keys at any time but can commit them only after governance calls stateToCommitting(), as proposals 5 and 17 and Arbitrum tasks 1 and 4 did; all four helpers were back in the setting state when checked.

Arbitrum: ProxyAdmin 0xb00a75949806158a90A86f70B4d4393619A4D527 and Delegator 0xbB7d93eF65F4131eD13aeE0497503d57ff74Ccfa answer to ArbitrumExecutor 0xc480F68A3dcC3EdD82134FAB45C14A0FcF1dA3CC, which runs a task only after ArbitrumSender 0x20Fa11c4F794eC1db3527bF618B02754FF393bD5 on Ethereum, owned by the L1 Delegator, marks it ready; tasks expire after 40 days.
limits: Only the Delegator owner can grant permissions. Every proposal of the Ethereum Voting contracts 0xfc4B580C9bda2EEf4E94D9Fb4bcB1F7a61660cf9 and 0xc480F68A3dcC3EdD82134FAB45C14A0FcF1dA3CC and every Arbitrum executor task was decoded: none adds a safety vector, and the only grants still live are the four key helpers’ rights. A scan of 910 candidate callers, including four deployer accounts and the contracts each created at its first 150 to 400 nonces, found no other permission. Grants the deployer made while it owned each Delegator cannot be listed without event logs, so an immediate upgrade, wildcard or safety-vector right is not excluded.

A vote that switches a key helper to committing approves the state change, not specific keys. While the helper stays in the setting state, its owner can change the staged keys until the vote executes and then commit them, or commit empty keys that delete a circuit’s verification key, with no further delay; moving the helper to the waiting state first freezes its keys for voters to check.
The 7-day governance delay is not an assured exit window: one safety-vector key can pause the proxy and block unshields until governance unpauses it.

Only the Ethereum and Arbitrum proxies are covered; the Polygon and BSC deployments, the Base executor 0xc73D11a8AD9062FC94Be26f3d1189159846B1E76 reached through OPStackSender 0x60698d5e9b6029048dE669fDFba25E77203Bf161 (proposal 27 readied its tasks 0 to 11), RelayAdapt, wallets, broadcasters and PPOI need their own review.
The Arbitrum ProxyAdmin has no Sourcify match; its owner and function selectors were checked on chain against the verified Ethereum ProxyAdmin.
Circuit soundness and the trusted setup were not audited; verification keys remain replaceable through governance and the key helpers.

The original 0.5.11 pools keep onlyOperator functions, including verifier replacement, but operator() returns the zero address, so no caller can pass that check; the later 0.7.6 pools have no operator and fix their verifier, hasher, token and denomination at deployment. The verifiers and hashers are nonproxy code that only compute. Anyone can submit a withdrawal with a valid proof against a recent root, with no relayer, router or governance step. TORN governance, captured in May 2023, controls only the periphery and cannot move pool funds or block a direct withdrawal.
controls: No pool administrator: operator() is the zero address in the 0.5.11 pools, which disables their onlyOperator functions (updateVerifier, changeOperator and the 0.1 ETH pool’s finished migration calls); the 0.7.6 pools have no such functions.
TORN governance controls the upgradeable InstanceRegistry and relayer registry, which gate only the optional router and relayer path, not direct calls to the pools.
In the cDAI pools anyone can send accrued COMP rewards to TORN governance; the pooled cDAI stays in the pool.
limits: D0 covers only the listed pool addresses. Retired pools whose operator is still live can have their verifier replaced: the early mixer 0x94A1B5CdB22c43faab4AbEb5c74999895464Ddaf (EOA operator) and eight pools whose operator is multisig 0xDD4c48C0B24039969fC16D1cdF626eaB821d3384. None held funds when checked.
Relayers, the router and interfaces are optional and not graded; a direct withdrawal requires building the proof locally and paying gas.
Circuit soundness and the trusted-setup ceremony are cryptographic assumptions this review did not audit.
Pooled-token issuers and governors (USDC, USDT, WBTC, DAI and Compound's cDAI) keep their own controls, which compose through each holding's asset review.
canonicalAddresses records only the 100 ETH pool on each chain; the immutable identity lists every reviewed pool.
